stances:Trade and tariffs:1.text: Responded to a threat to double tariffs on Mexico. “Tariffs should be a tool to level the playing field for American workers and businesses, not a weapon to scapegoat immigrants or settle political scores.”
stances:Trade and tariffs:1.evidence: 2026-11-16: Sánchez on Trump’s latest Mexico tariff threat

stances:Trade and tariffs:2.text: Joined Los Angeles County colleagues for a roundtable on trade policy at the Port of Los Angeles. “It’s clear that President Trump’s chaotic trade policies are hurting Americans”
stances:Trade and tariffs:2.evidence: 2026-10-29: Sánchez, L.A. County members spotlight cost of Trump’s trade polices at Port of Los Angeles

stances:Trade and tariffs:3.text: Criticized a round of tariffs the administration said were meant to combat forced labor. “We need to take forced labor seriously.”
stances:Trade and tariffs:3.evidence: 2026-07-23: Sánchez: Trump’s latest tariffs aren’t serious attempt to combat forced labor

stances:Immigration and taxpayer data:1.text: Led a bicameral amicus brief on IRS-to-ICE taxpayer address sharing. “led 85 House and Senate Democrats in filing a bicameral amicus brief urging the U.S. Court of Appeals for the First Circuit to uphold a lower court’s order blocking Immigration and Customs Enforcement from using – or even viewing – tens of thousands of taxpayers’ addresses obtained from the IRS”
stances:Immigration and taxpayer data:1.evidence: 2026-07-30: Sánchez, CHC colleagues lead amicus brief in fight over IRS-ICE taxpayer data sharing

stances:Immigration and taxpayer data:2.text: Voted against the Laken Riley Act (H.R. 29). It passed 264–159.
stances:Immigration and taxpayer data:2.evidence: Roll 2025-6 (H R 29, 2025-01-07): Sánchez Nay; total 264–159; Democrats 48–159; Passed

stances:Health care and Medicaid:1.text: Voted against the Do No Harm in Medicaid Act (H.R. 498). It passed 215–201.
stances:Health care and Medicaid:1.evidence: Roll 2025-362 (H R 498, 2025-12-18): Sánchez Nay; total 215–201; Democrats 4–201; Passed

stances:Health care and Medicaid:2.text: Voted against H.R. 1, the reconciliation bill the Clerk lists as the One Big Beautiful Act. It passed 215–214.
stances:Health care and Medicaid:2.evidence: Roll 2025-145 (H R 1, 2025-05-22): Sánchez Nay; total 215–214; Democrats 0–212; Passed

stances:Housing and Social Security:1.text: Introduced the Protecting Our Widows and Widowers in Retirement (POWR) Act. “After decades of hard work and paying into the system, widows and widowers deserve to keep the benefits they earned together.”
stances:Housing and Social Security:1.evidence: 2026-09-02: Sánchez introduces bill to strengthen Social Security benefits for widows, widowers

stances:Housing and Social Security:2.text: Introduced the bipartisan Rental Housing Investment Act. “Southern California families are being priced out of their own communities”
stances:Housing and Social Security:2.evidence: 2026-05-21: Bipartisan bill would tackle rental housing shortage, lower costs for families

stances:Israel and Palestine:1.text: Cosponsored the Block the Bombs Act, saying “I oppose providing offensive weapons to Prime Minister Netanyahu and his far-right government without meaningful safeguards or accountability.”
stances:Israel and Palestine:1.evidence: 2026-07-14: Sánchez cosponsors Block the Bombs Act

stances:Israel and Palestine:2.text: In the same statement: “While I have consistently supported defensive aid for close American allies, military aid for Israel must include strong conditions to prevent further suffering.”
stances:Israel and Palestine:2.evidence: 2026-07-14: Sánchez cosponsors Block the Bombs Act
